scope: Ten original prior LIMITED_SOURCE 215-bank items; 40 option verdicts source-read against current MA/Federal official rule text; AI review, NOT licensed human external certification

items.decision: RI-issued nonnarcotic CII valid and presented initially within five calendar days, then same-pharmacy patient-requested remainder up to thirty days after issue; Nov4→Nov8 initial and Nov27 remainder both qualify.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: 72h is the separate stock shortage pathway, not patient-request remainder.
Both five-day first presentation and thirty-day same-pharmacy remainder deadlines are met.
MA permits qualifying out-of-state patient-requested CII partials.
Properly documented lawful partial-fill does not itself demand a new prescription.

items.decision: Unfilled original EPCS II–V transfers only once in native electronic form; Schedule VI unfilled oral/paper/fax/electronic transferable under state rule; paper controlled original is not magically converted to EPCS.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: One-time transfer of genuine unfilled electronic CII for initial dispense is permitted.
Scanned paper CIV is not an original EPCS and this pathway does not permit transfer.
MA permits oral never-filled Schedule VI transfer under 247 CMR9 provisions.
Second initial-dispense electronic transfer of the same CIII original exceeds one-time rule.

items.decision: Emergency oral CII pharmacist reduces order to writing, authenticates, and practitioner delivers written or compliant electronic follow-up within seven calendar days of oral authorization; report missing follow-up to DEA.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Seven business days is longer than federal seven-day limit and cannot displace it.
Federal deadline is seven calendar days plus specific follow-up/emergency annotations.
72-hour partial stock-shortage timing is unrelated to emergency CII oral Rx.
Pharmacist verification does not eliminate follow-up or failure notice.

items.decision: The Massachusetts 90-day CII/III exceptions cover nonopioids such as methylphenidate, OUD treatments, and infusion pumps; routine opioid analgesics remain at 30 days.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: ADHD methylphenidate is expressly named nonopioid exception to 90d maximum.
Hydrocodone/APAP analgesia is a routine opioid analgesic not qualifying here.
Codeine analgesia is not nonopioid or OUD treatment and is capped at 30d.
Buprenorphine analgesic patch for pain does not qualify solely by drug name for OUD exception.

items.decision: Dispensers report II–V outpatient fills and gabapentin within 24h or next business day following last transmission; nonresident delivery to Massachusetts covered; inpatient medication order exception; prescriber query exemption separate.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Outpatient Schedule IV alprazolam is covered with 24h/next-business-day reporting timing.
Nonresident pharmacy delivery of tramadol CIV to MA resident is covered.
Hospital inpatient medication orders are expressly excluded from pharmacy PMP report.
Prescriber hospice query waiver does not itself cancel the dispenser report obligation.

items.law: MA Vaccine Administration Policy 2023-02 rev 2025 §IV(D)–(F); CDC VIS
items.decision: Adult zoster under valid standing order may be selected/administered by qualified pharmacist; MIIS must be checked before non-influenza/non-COVID vaccines, VIS before shot, tech trainees excluded.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Qualified pharmacist plus valid standing order and patient screening fits authorized workflow.
Zoster vaccine is neither influenza nor COVID; MIIS pre-administration check required.
Technician trainee is expressly excluded from authorized pharmacy vaccinators.
VIS must be furnished before, not after, vaccine administration.

items.decision: DEA opened CII exact count; opened CIII-V >1,000 tablets original container exact count; a 1,000-tab CIV container can be estimated; expired CII remains in inventory/perpetual records until lawful removal.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Opened 2,000-tablet CIII original must be exact; expired CII not removed prematurely.
CII + >1000-capacity CIII exact, 1000-capacity CIV may be estimated; expired CII inventoried.
Electronic records do not dispense with physical count nor retained expired controlled stock.
Even exact-counting CIV voluntarily does not permit excluding on-hand expired CII.

items.decision: Federal DEA notice of actual theft/significant loss within one business day, Form106 follow-up; Board Policy 2026-01 requires RLCS and Form106 if applicable within seven calendar days, theft any quantity.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Delay to next inventory/licensure is incompatible with federal and state deadlines.
One business day DEA written notice and state seven-calendar-day RLCS/Form106 workflow fit.
State reporting alone does not substitute for DEA notification.
Confirmed theft remains reportable even if product later recovered.

items.law: M.G.L. c112 §12D; 105 CMR720; MA midstream interchange policy; DPH DCP22-01-112
items.decision: Cheaper available interchangeable product required absent no-substitution; prescriber must issue new no-substitution Rx to prevent future midstream interchange; FDA authorized generics equivalent to own brands despite no separate Orange Book listing.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Interchange duty generally applies to less-expensive available listed equivalent without no-substitution.
Valid prescriber no-substitution overrides routine lower-cost interchange.
A new properly marked no-substitution Rx is the mechanism for preventing midstream interchange.
DPH says authorized generic may replace brand without distinct Orange Book listing if not prohibited.

items.decision: Prescriptions for minors generally limited to seven-day opiate supply, but documented practitioner's medical-necessity exception applies to acute conditions when other requirements met and nonopiate alternatives found inappropriate.

choice_verdicts.independent_reason: Law expressly includes a medical-necessity exception even for minors.
Cancer/palliative are examples, not exclusive; acute condition is separately authorized.
Documented acute medical-necessity path permits ten-day opioid order on assumptions.
Pharmacist cannot independently extend seven to ten days solely on parent's consent.
